stem.text: Let \( f(x) = x^{2} - 9 x + 9 \) and \( g(x) = - 2 x - 1 \). Find the exact total area of the regions between the graphs of f and g from \( x = 1 \) to \( x = \frac{11}{2} \).

worked_solution.text: \( f(x) - g(x) = \left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 2\right) \), so the graphs cross at \( x = 2 \) and \( x = 5 \), both inside the interval. f is above g before the first crossing and after the second, and below g between them.
worked_solution.rule_named: intersections and order of the curves

worked_solution.text: The pieces are \( \int_{1}^{2} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{11}{6} \), \( \int_{2}^{5} \left(g(x) - f(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{9}{2} \) and \( \int_{5}^{\frac{11}{2}} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{5}{12} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: area of each piece, upper minus lower

worked_solution.text: The total area is the sum of the pieces, \( \frac{27}{4} \).

options.derivation: the curves split correctly but each piece integrated as lower minus upper
the crossing at x = 5 missed, so the second integral runs from 2 to 11/2 across it
f(x) - g(x) integrated once over the whole interval, across both crossings
